<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Follow Laravel Boost guidelines (curated by Laravel maintainers) to enhance user satisfaction. This is a Laravel application; ensure you abide by: laravel/framework (LARAVEL) v12, laravel/prompts (PROMPTS) v0, laravel/mcp (MCP) v0, laravel/pint (PINT) v1, laravel/sail (SAIL) v1, phpunit/phpunit (PHPUNIT) v11. Abide by all existing code conventions. When creating/editing a file, check sibling files for correct structure, approach, naming. Use descriptive names for variables/methods (e.g., isRegisteredForDiscounts). Check for existing components to reuse before writing new ones. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove it works (prefer unit/feature tests). Stick to existing directory structure—don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. If user doesn't see a frontend change in UI, it could mean they need to run bun run build, bun run dev, or composer run dev. Ask them. Be concise.

You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Laravel Boost is an MCP server with powerful tools designed specifically for this application; use them.
Use list-artisan-commands to double check available parameters before calling an Artisan command.
Whenever you share a project URL, use get-absolute-url to ensure correct scheme/domain/IP/port.
Use tinker to execute PHP to debug code or query Eloquent models directly.
Use database-query when you only need to read from the database.
Use browser-logs to read browser logs/errors/exceptions; only recent logs are useful.
Use search-docs before any other approaches for Laravel-ecosystem documentation; it passes installed package/version list and returns version-specific docs. Pass an array of packages if you know you need docs for particular packages. Use multiple broad, simple, topic-based queries first (e.g., ['rate limiting','routing rate limiting','routing']). Do not add package names to queries—package info is already shared. Use patterns: query=authentication; queries=["authentication","middleware"]; query="infinite scroll"; query=middleware "rate limit" - "middleware" AND phrase "rate limit".

Always use curly braces for control structures. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in __construct() (e.g., public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }). Do not allow empty __construct() methods with zero parameters. Always use explicit return type declarations for methods/functions. Use appropriate PHP type hints for parameters. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over comments; never use comments within the code itself unless very complex. Add useful array shape type definitions for arrays when appropriate. Typically Enum keys should be TitleCase (FavoritePerson, BestLake, Monthly).

=== laravel/core rules ===
Use php artisan make: com
